articles.title: Hydraulic Barrier Optimization Using Random‐Walk Particle Tracking in Heterogeneous Media: Effects of Dispersion, Particle Discretization and Algorithmic Initialization
articles.titleEn: Hydraulic Barrier Optimization Using Random‐Walk Particle Tracking in Heterogeneous Media: Effects of Dispersion, Particle Discretization and Algorithmic Initialization
articles.abstract: Hydraulic barriers (HBs) are commonly used for solute plume containment in polluted aquifers. Their long‐term sustainability depends on minimizing the cumulative pumping rate, , required to ensure plume capture. Lagrangian random‐walk particle tracking (RWPT) is an effective approach for simulating advective‐dispersive transport to wells. However, as this method typically requires a large number of particles, , RWPT‐based simulation–optimization (SO) can be computationally demanding. This work presents an SO framework that couples a warm‐start genetic algorithm with parallel RWPT to identify minimal pumping rates for HB containment in a computationally efficient manner. The framework was applied in a Monte Carlo study using stochastic hydraulic conductivity fields, with ranging from to . Results showed that optimal values were jointly conditioned by transport processes, particle discretization, and algorithmic initialization. Under advection‐only transport, was nearly insensitive to . In contrast, when local dispersion was included, and its variability increased with . The influence of particle discretization depended strongly on the adopted recovery criterion, becoming substantially weaker when incomplete particle recovery was allowed. Neglecting local dispersion can therefore underestimate pumping requirements, particularly under stringent recovery criteria and increasing particle resolution. Warm‐start initialization generally identified lower solutions than cold initialization while also reducing computational time. These findings demonstrate that particle discretization, local dispersion and the recovery criterion should be considered explicitly when optimizing HBs, and that warm‐start strategies can substantially improve computational efficiency in RWPT‐based SO workflows.

articles.title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO 2
articles.titleEn: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO 2
articles.abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO 2 . We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO 2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana , to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO 2 . L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana , increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO 2 —at the experimental peatland. L. laricina 's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana 's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO 2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.

articles.title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
articles.titleEn: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO 2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO 2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO 2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

articles.title: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
articles.titleEn: Predicting protein electrostatics with protein language models
articles.abstract: Ionization states are crucial to protein function, yet predicting their equilibrium constants remains challenging. Here we present KaML-ESMs, sequence-based neural networks built on the ESM protein language models and trained on the GAINES-augmented PKAD-3r dataset. KaML-ESM2/ESMC outperform alternative approaches across four benchmarks, achieving root-mean-square errors of about 0.5 units for Asp/Glu/His/Cys/Tyr/Lys residues in native proteins. Performance degrades on 89 buried engineered mutations lacking evolutionary support, revealing a limitation that supervised training may help overcome. These results suggest that protein sequence, through its evolutionary context, encodes not only structure and function but also, indirectly, electrostatic characteristics. Applying KaML-ESM2 to the entire human proteome, we show that predicted p K a values can identify functional sites and infer catalytic mechanisms. We offer KaML, a sequence-based p K a prediction platform supporting biological exploration, protein engineering, and biomolecular simulation. With further development, GAINES could provide a general framework for addressing data scarcity in machine learning.

articles.title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
articles.titleEn: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

articles.title: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
articles.titleEn: Phylogenomics of captured Cryptosporidium sequenced directly from patient samples identifies clade-specific genomic architecture and host-adapted lineages
articles.abstract: Cryptosporidium causes diarrhea and high mortality in young children in Africa and southern Asia. Low oocyst counts in stool often limit whole-genome sequencing from clinical samples. Here, we enrich for Cryptosporidium genomic DNA directly from stool samples using 74,973 RNA baits (CryptoCap_75K; 8.2 Mb) derived from gene-rich areas (100% coding capacity) within the Cryptosporidium parvum genome. This method produces genome-wide sequence data with sufficient depth and breadth of coverage using as few as 25 oocysts, including divergent species such as Cryptosporidium ubiquitum . To minimize reference bias, we utilize a dual-mapping strategy that integrates reads aligned to both C. parvum and C. ubiquitum to capture lineage-specific variation. Phylogenetic networks, haplotypes, and admixture analyses identify three C. ubiquitum groups, A and B exclusive to humans, with B showing evidence of admixture, whereas C is zoonotic. Group-specific polymorphisms cluster within discrete genomic regions, suggesting conserved haploblocks associate with host adaptation. This capture-based genomics approach provides high-resolution insights into Cryptosporidium population genetics and lays the groundwork for studies of zoonotic transmission, anthroponosis, and GWAS directly from clinical material.

articles.title: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
articles.titleEn: Exsolution of metal nanoparticles by control of point defects
articles.abstract: Exsolution involves redox precipitation of metal nanoparticles from metal oxides, resulting in materials that exhibit excellent electrocatalytic properties and hold great promise for novel types of nanoscale heterostructures. However, a coherent understanding of the phenomenon is lacking. Here, exsolution is described by three point defect equations involving the reduction of the host oxide, reduction and exsolution of the transition metal, and annihilation of host unit cells. Guided by their predictions, significantly enhanced exsolution in terms of molar amount, rate, and nucleation density is achieved by acceptor substitution in the system La 0.2 Ca 0.7 Ti 0.95 Cu 0.05 O 3− δ , as shown by atomic scale imaging and in situ X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy. It is demonstrated that the oxygen stoichiometry of the parent oxide increases upon exsolution despite oxygen loss in the reducing environment. Furthermore, strain in both the host oxide and the exsolved metal can constitute an additional thermodynamic barrier for exsolution beyond the availability of the required point defects.

articles.title: Urbanization Amplifies Regional Precipitation Contrasts but not Urban‐Core Precipitation Extremes
articles.titleEn: Urbanization Amplifies Regional Precipitation Contrasts but not Urban‐Core Precipitation Extremes
articles.abstract: Urbanization is often assumed to intensify precipitation and concentrate flood‐relevant extremes in city centers, yet clear observational evidence remains limited. Here, we analyze warm‐season sub‐daily precipitation during 2000–2024 across 20 urban agglomerations and 61 representative cities in China, partitioning built‐up areas into three urban‐intensity zones based on impervious surface fraction. Total precipitation generally increases more rapidly in urban areas than in nearby non‐urban reference regions, with about 75% of urban agglomerations showing faster urban wetting. However, this enhancement is primarily driven by light‐to‐moderate precipitation, for which urbanization effects strengthen systematically from weakly to highly urbanized zones. Quantitatively, urban‐intensity sensitivity is positive for non‐extreme precipitation, with urbanization effects increasing by about 0.1–0.7 mm yr −1 for each 10% increase in impervious surface fraction, but it becomes negative for extremes, decreasing on average by about 0.5–1.1 mm yr −1 . Accordingly, only 20%–25% of urban agglomerations show stronger amplification of extreme precipitation in highly urbanized zones, whereas roughly one‐third show weaker or negative urbanization effects in these zones. These patterns are consistent at the city scale, are more evident at hourly than daily resolution, and are strongest in humid regions. Our results show that stronger urbanization amplifies regional precipitation contrasts but does not systematically amplify precipitation extremes in urban cores, challenging a common assumption in urban flood‐risk assessment and emphasizing the need to distinguish general urban wetting from changes in short‐duration hazardous rainfall.

articles.title: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
articles.titleEn: Single-cell–level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies
articles.abstract: Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type–specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell–level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO’s digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4 + T cells.

articles.title: Integrating ecology with genetics to explain gene reuse during repeated evolution
articles.titleEn: Integrating ecology with genetics to explain gene reuse during repeated evolution
articles.abstract: The role of determinism and chance in the evolutionary history of life is often analyzed through the lens of the repeatability of evolution. Although it is now clear that evolution often repeats itself, we are only beginning to understand why this varies in degree. For example, the probability of gene reuse during repeated bouts of adaptation often declines with time since divergence, but the causes of this pattern remain unclear. Here, we explore two core hypotheses for time-dependent variation in the repeatability of gene reuse during adaptation. Specifically, gene reuse depends on the extent to which lineages have 1) similar genomes such that they have similar genetic architectures, mutations, and mutational effects (i.e., a fairly well-appreciated “shared genetics” hypothesis), and 2) similar ecologies such that they have similar environments and patterns of natural selection (i.e., a mostly unexplored “shared ecology” hypothesis). The latter hypothesis emphasizes ecology’s role in gene reuse and has received little explicit attention. In particular, testing the shared ecology hypothesis requires moving beyond a simple dichotomous characterization of ecology to embracing ecological divergence as a multivariate and continuous phenomenon. Although such tests are only beginning to emerge, they already illustrate how integration of ecological factors can help explain variation in gene reuse. Here, we advocate a framework that integrates the influence of both genetic and ecological factors in the repeatability of evolution and can be applied to a range of organisms to better understand the role of determinism and chance in biological diversification.

articles.title: High-resolution measurements of thermal conductivity matrix and search for thermal Hall effect in La 2 CuO 4
articles.titleEn: High-resolution measurements of thermal conductivity matrix and search for thermal Hall effect in La 2 CuO 4
articles.abstract: We investigated the longitudinal thermal conductivity κ xx and thermal Hall conductivity κ xy in La 2 CuO 4 at temperatures T between 2 and 20 K in magnetic fields H up to 10 T. Within the temperature and field intervals studied, we do not resolve any thermal Hall signal with a conservative upper bound of | κ xy / T | 1 × 10 − 4 Wm − 1 K − 2 . The longitudinal thermal conductivity κ xx / T agrees well with previous reports, in both its magnitude and T dependence. Both κ xx and κ xy were measured using the field-swept protocol. To achieve high resolution, we carefully took into account relaxation effects after each step-increase in H . At low T , we find a weak linear decrease in κ xx / T vs. H , as well as weak hystereses near the metamagnetic transitions of the spins.

articles.title: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification
articles.titleEn: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification
articles.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is constrained by rapid RNA degradation during sample storage, necessitating cold-chain logistics. Here we present spatially confined biosilicification (SCB), wherein RNA is encapsulated within a nanoscopic layer of amorphous silicon dioxide, as a highly effective methodology enabling ambient-temperature preservation of single-cell transcriptomes. By judiciously incorporating a silicification inhibitor, SCB achieves spatiotemporal control over both intra- and extracellular silica deposition, preventing excessive crosslinking and cell aggregation while preserving RNA biointegrity and accessibility. scRNA-seq performed with biosilicified cells (Si-scRNA-seq) maintained high transcriptomic fidelity with fresh samples (R 2 = 0.95 after 7 d) extending RNA half-life to 54.8 d at 25 °C, a 685-fold improvement compared to unprotected samples. Furthermore, Si-scRNA-seq confers robust resistance against oxidative and UV degradation. Compatible with mainstream platforms at ~0.1 RMB per sample, Si-scRNA-seq successfully resolves cellular heterogeneity in clinical lung, liver, and ovarian cancer specimens after extended room-temperature storage. Si-scRNA-seq provides a scalable and cold-chain–free solution for single-cell transcriptomics in research and clinical settings.

articles.title: Education reduces dementia incidence and mitigates genetic risk
articles.titleEn: Education reduces dementia incidence and mitigates genetic risk
articles.abstract: There is little causal evidence on factors that can protect individuals against Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) risk. We study the causal effect of education on ADRD, exploiting a regression discontinuity generated by a compulsory schooling reform. ADRD was ascertained based on medical history, hospital records, and death registries, addressing concerns about selective sample attrition. We find that education reduces incidence of ADRD. Using molecular genetic data, we show that the reform weakened the relationship between genetics and ADRD incidence, implying genetic risk of dementia is not immutable and can be modified by social policy.
articles.abstractEn: There is little causal evidence on factors that can protect individuals against Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) risk. We study the causal effect of education on ADRD, exploiting a regression discontinuity generated by a compulsory schooling reform. ADRD was ascertained based on medical history, hospital records, and death registries, addressing concerns about selective sample attrition. We find that education reduces incidence of ADRD. Using molecular genetic data, we show that the reform weakened the relationship between genetics and ADRD incidence, implying genetic risk of dementia is not immutable and can be modified by social policy.

articles.title: Integrating a global glacier model into local hydrological modeling: Impacts on melt contributions
articles.titleEn: Integrating a global glacier model into local hydrological modeling: Impacts on melt contributions
articles.abstract: Snow and glacier meltwater are critical water resources for mountain regions, yet their accurate representation in hydrological models remains challenging. As climate change alters the timing and magnitude of melt contributions, accurate partitioning between snow and glacier sources becomes increasingly important. To address this challenge, this study couples the hydrological model HBV (as implemented in the Raven modeling framework) with the Global Glacier Evolution Model GloGEM and integrates a snow redistribution scheme for application across 14 glaciated headwater catchments in Switzerland. At this local catchment scale, we investigate whether glacier constraints and the addition of snow redistribution reduce parameter equifinality and increase the reliability of melt contribution estimates. Simulations are evaluated against observed streamflow, gridded snow water equivalent data, and glacier melt data based on observed mass balance. The gravitational snow redistribution algorithm successfully prevents unrealistic high-elevation snow accumulation and improves catchment average SWE simulation performance. Uncoupled HBV configurations outperform coupled HBV-GloGEM setups according to streamflow metrics. However, this superior performance is achieved by simulating glacier melt rates exceeding GloGEM estimates and glacier storage change data by factors of 2–3 in some catchments, effectively using glacier ice to offset precipitation biases in forcing data, which can be critical for climate change impact studies. Within a single model configuration, glacier melt contributions can vary by more than a factor of three among the best-performing parameter sets, and by up to an order of magnitude in weakly glacierized catchments, highlighting severe parameter equifinality. Coupling the HBV model with GloGEM (calibrated using glacier-specific geodetic mass balance) produces glacier melt consistent with observations and substantially improves identifiability of both glacier and snowmelt contributions. Despite lower streamflow performance metrics, glacier melt constraints prevent compensatory errors that would compromise projections as melt dynamics shift under climate change. Applying this framework to future climate scenarios and integrating additional constraints such as snow observations may further improve the reliability of melt contribution projections.

articles.title: Characterizing Climate-Driven Shifts in Chilean Rainfall Regimes with a Hybrid Hidden Markov–Copula Framework
articles.titleEn: Characterizing Climate-Driven Shifts in Chilean Rainfall Regimes with a Hybrid Hidden Markov–Copula Framework
articles.abstract: Chile's hydroclimate exhibits pronounced meridional gradients and strong interannual variability, posing persistent challenges for regime-aware, probabilistic rainfall prediction. articles.title: Process-based upgrades to the WRF multi-layer green-roof scheme (WRF-MLGR v2.0) and evaluation against field observations
articles.titleEn: Process-based upgrades to the WRF multi-layer green-roof scheme (WRF-MLGR v2.0) and evaluation against field observations
articles.abstract: Green roofs can moderate urban heat by increasing latent heat flux and reducing sensible heat flux. However, capturing these effects in models depends on accurate representation of key green-roof processes, including substrate heat and moisture transport, soil-vegetation-atmosphere energy and moisture exchanges, interactions with the underlying roof, and drainage. Here we introduce targeted, process-based updates to the green-roof scheme (hereafter, MLGR) within the multi-layer urban canopy model (BEP-BEM) in the WRF mesoscale model to address key limitations in the original formulation. The updates include a non-linear dependence of soil thermal conductivity on moisture, vegetation-modulated surface thermal conductivity, explicit soil-surface evaporation, multi-layer root water uptake for transpiration, and canopy interception with evaporation and dew formation. We evaluate the original and modified MLGR schemes using hourly observations from an extensive sedum roof in London, Canada, for “summer” (1 July–31 August 2014) and “fall” (1 September–31 October 2014) periods. We also analyze 11–18 October 2025, when green roof modules were placed directly on the roof deck – which corresponds to the model's lower boundary assumption. Following implementation of the process-based improvements, model–measurement agreement for the conductive heat flux is markedly improved: RMSE is reduced from 105.9 to 24.0 W m −2 in summer and from 94.2 to 24.0 W m −2 in fall and the model produces more realistic overall green roof energy partitioning. The modified model better captures post-rain increases in latent heat flux ( Q E ) and improves the timing and magnitude of daytime turbulent latent and sensible heat flux peaks ( Q E and Q H ). Drainage is reduced relative to the original scheme; however, it remains slightly underestimated during summer and slightly overestimated during fall, and biases persist in surface temperature (warm during the day and cool at night) and in the magnitude and variability of Q E . Overall, the revised MLGR physics improves surface-flux realism, and future development should focus on developing a more realistic vegetation canopy submodule.

articles.title: Unexpected land-surface warming following a relatively limited-forcing hypothetical nuclear war
articles.titleEn: Unexpected land-surface warming following a relatively limited-forcing hypothetical nuclear war
articles.abstract: Nuclear conflicts could ignite intense fires that inject considerable amounts of black carbon (BC) into the upper troposphere and lower stratosphere, with the potential to disrupt global climate. While uncertainties in the BC injection remain large, relatively few modeling studies have explored the climatic response to more limited nuclear exchange between major nuclear powers. Here, we investigate the climate response to a set of relatively limited-forcing scenarios (12 to 24 Tg BC) for nuclear exchanges between the United States and Russia. This corresponds to one-tenth to one-fifth of the forcing strength of typically considered. We use the Canadian Earth System Model version 5, an independent contributor to the worldwide set of Earth System Models that has not been explored previously in this application. Consistent with previous work, decreased downwelling shortwave radiation at the surface drives prolonged surface cooling. Unexpectedly, however, a transient surface warming develops in the first boreal summer following a boreal-winter injection, linked to reduced cooling via net longwave and turbulent fluxes. The transient warming is most pronounced for the lowest forcing cases. Precipitation, which decreases even while the surface warms, is found to be controlled by stabilizing, top-heavy warming. Multi-model assessment of these relatively limited-forcing cases is warranted given their potential impacts.

articles.title: Timing of the anthropogenic carbon invasion in the Southern California Current
articles.titleEn: Timing of the anthropogenic carbon invasion in the Southern California Current
articles.abstract: The Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems (EBUS), such as the Southern California Current System (CCS), are well-known high-productivity regions driven by alongshore winds, although their role as oceanic sources and sinks of atmospheric CO 2 in the global carbon cycle is poorly understood. In the southern CCS, off Baja California, wind-driven vertical mixing upwells nutrient and carbon-rich waters from late winter to early summer, while weaker winds during the rest of the year allow the intrusion of nutrients and carbon-depleted subtropical surface waters. Here, we interpret the isotopic composition of organic carbon and calcitic records spanning ∼ 160 years from high-resolution sediment cores collected off Baja California, showing a clear trend toward lighter carbon isotopic compositions of the organic and inorganic carbon for the past seven decades. These trends are similar to the atmospheric records associated with the 13 C Suess effect, suggesting an atmospheric carbon invasion into the surface waters of the California Current. Nevertheless, the slope of the atmospheric carbon isotopic records is steeper than our marine record, most likely related to the upward mixing of subsurface waters with a relatively heavier carbon isotopic signature and advection processes inherent to the strong seasonality of the CCS southern boundary. These results will allow a better characterization of the relative role of the EBUS regions in the global carbon cycle.

articles.title: Fine-scale spatial variability of winter CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes in Arctic tundra derived from snowpack gradient measurements
articles.titleEn: Fine-scale spatial variability of winter CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes in Arctic tundra derived from snowpack gradient measurements
articles.abstract: Winter carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) fluxes from soils under seasonal snowpacks make non-negligible, yet poorly constrained contributions to annual carbon budgets across Arctic regions. Quantifying these fluxes and their spatial variance will better constrain uncertainties in simulations of winter carbon fluxes from terrestrial biosphere models. We address this gap by measuring and identifying patterns and spatial variability in CO 2 and CH 4 soil-atmosphere fluxes through late winter snowpacks at an upland tundra site in the western Canadian Arctic. Instantaneous fluxes were calculated from CO 2 and CH 4 microsite concentration gradients at 10 to 20 cm vertical resolution ( n =119) through the snowpack across five homogeneous surface covers, representing dominant vegetation types. We measured consistent soil-to-atmosphere CO 2 fluxes but with significantly different rates across surface covers (0.8 to 100 mgC m −2 d −1 ), which were strongly influenced by snow depth and soil surface temperature, exhibiting higher emissions under deeper snowpacks and warmer soil surfaces. CH 4 fluxes were also coupled to soil surface temperature and varied between −0.04 and 0.08 mgC m −2 d −1 . Persistent CH 4 uptake was observed in warmer soils (−6.0 to −0.5 °C) in a sparsely populated black spruce and shrub dominated area with deep snow, indicating active methane oxidation during winter. Microsite scale CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes were statistically independent of vertical snow microstructure, indicating that winter fluxes could be reliably calculated from single gas concentration at the soil-snow interface, negating the need for additional snowpack gas measurements. These results open new avenues for quantifying fine-scale spatial variability of wintertime CO 2 and CH 4 fluxes in Arctic tundra, which can constrain biogeochemical process representations in terrestrial biosphere models and inform spatial upscaling methodologies.

articles.title: Human and climate-environment interactions in Pyrenean landscapes: a Lateglacial-Holocene multiproxy reconstruction
articles.titleEn: Human and climate-environment interactions in Pyrenean landscapes: a Lateglacial-Holocene multiproxy reconstruction
articles.abstract: Mountain ecosystems present a complex challenge in disentangling the drivers of their long-term transformation. The subalpine belt of the Pyrenees, once forested, is now characterised by a mosaic of forest patches and open landscapes, and has represented a key region in herding practices until the last century, when land-use changes have led to a reforestation of this area. However, the relative contributions of climate and human activity in driving its change remain intensely contested. We present a high-resolution, multi-proxy reconstruction of landscape dynamics over the last 25 000 years from the southern Pyrenees. We have integrated mammal herbivores, fire regime and vegetation dynamics through sedimentary ancient DNA, pollen and charcoal analyses. With this approach, we aim to compare these proxies and identify the timing and drivers of vegetation change and to distinguish anthropogenic from climatic forces. Our results reveal a multi-phase evolution, with Lateglacial and postglacial forest expansion followed by Mid-Holocene openness, initially triggered by the cooling at the initial phase of the Neoglacial period, but subsequently maintained by pastoral activities. We find that humans opportunistically exploited this openness from the Mid-Holocene onwards, later transitioning to active landscape management through fires and grazing. This study demonstrates that current Pyrenean landscapes are not a product of exclusively humans or climate, but of their synergy over millennia. Effective conservation strategies must integrate an understanding of this deep ecological history with the emulation of traditional practices to preserve these unique, human-shaped biodiversity hotspots.

articles.title: Flood exposure and structure damage under deterministic design-storm and stochastic storm transposition rainfall scenarios: a case study in South Louisiana, USA
articles.titleEn: Flood exposure and structure damage under deterministic design-storm and stochastic storm transposition rainfall scenarios: a case study in South Louisiana, USA
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Flood hazard maps and damage estimates guide floodplain management, mitigation planning, and engineering design, but they commonly rely on rainfall frequency analysis to define annual exceedance probability (AEP) storms, commonly referred to as design storms. Current engineering practice typically employs spatially uniform design storms derived from point-based gauge statistics; however, this approach suppresses the spatial organization and intensity gradients present in observed storms. Stochastic storm transposition (SST) offers an alternative by preserving the spatial structure of observed rainfall and stochastically repositioning full storm fields across a watershed. This study compares flood exposure and damage produced by Atlas 14 and SST rainfall representations in the Vermilion River Basin, a low-gradient inland–coastal watershed in south-central Louisiana. Although the TP40-adjusted Atlas 14 rainfall depth was larger than the mean basin-average SST accumulation across the 50 realizations (310 mm vs. 238.1 mm), the SST max composite produced substantially greater total structure damage than the baseline Atlas 14 scenario (USD 0.923 billion vs. USD 0.477 billion). Moreover, the comparison identified 11 518 buildings that were inundated in at least one SST realization but not under Atlas 14, representing more than USD 110 million in cumulative structural damage. The divergence between the two approaches is concentrated in mid-elevation urban neighborhoods, where spatial rainfall variability can cross local inundation thresholds that were not crossed under the spatially uniform storm. These results show that, in the VRB, the spatially uniform Atlas 14 design storm missed localized flood exposure that emerged when storm placement and rainfall spatial variability were represented.

articles.title: Runout mechanism of landslides in alluvial basins with emphasis on the impact and erosion effects
articles.titleEn: Runout mechanism of landslides in alluvial basins with emphasis on the impact and erosion effects
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Landslide runout is a critical factor in risk assessment, and runout distance is the most widely used indicator of mobility. Runout distance is determined both by the landslide's initial conditions and through interactions with erodible substrates, which can affect momentum and inertia by altering basal friction and by increasing overall flow volume, generally increasing runout distance. During erosion, the landslide mass can exert sudden impact forces on the substrate at points where the slope changes abruptly. While erosion effects have been extensively discussed in prior studies, impact forces themselves have been overlooked. Here, we combine fieldwork in SE Tibet, laboratory tests, and numerical modelling to resolve the dynamics and effect of impact loading on landslides in alluvial basins. Impact-loading ring-shear tests and numerical simulations, backed up by field evidence, indicate that impact forces can near-instantaneously generate high excess pore water pressure within a saturated substrate, reducing basal friction of the landslide mass and extending runout. As density and geometry of the impactor determine a landslide impact force, both the impactor and substrate properties, including stiffness and compressibility, control the impact duration. The interplay of these two factors can lead to different landslide runout patterns and mobilities. The findings indicate that the farthest runout does not necessarily occur under the highest impact force; rather, an appropriate impact level exists that most effectively liquefies the substrate. The findings highlight the importance of considering substrate properties for both impact and erosion during landslide runout analyses, particularly those occurring in alluvial basins.

articles.title: Review article: Climate hazards in African cities – knowledge gaps and research needs
articles.titleEn: Review article: Climate hazards in African cities – knowledge gaps and research needs
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: This study conducts a semi-systematic assessment of scientific literature published between 2015 and 2025 to examine the current state of knowledge on climate hazards in African cities. A broad literature search yielded 1832 records, which were conservatively screened to a final sample of 272 articles. The corpus was analysed using quantitative mapping and a qualitative hazard-based expert review. The analysis reveals a rapidly expanding but uneven knowledge base. Research is geographically concentrated, with Central Africa and small and fast-growing secondary cities underrepresented. Flooding and heat-related topics dominate the literature, whereas sea-level rise, windstorms and urban water stress receive comparatively limited attention. Consideration of multiple hazards remains limited and uneven, while explicit analysis of interactions between hazards is rare. Earth Observation is widely used, but its broader potential remains underexploited, while high-resolution urban climate modelling and observations remain limited. Most studies focus on historical or present-day conditions, and few combine future climate scenarios with projected urban growth. Overall, broader geographic and thematic coverage, improved high-resolution observations and urban-scale modelling, and stronger integration of future climate and urban development are needed to provide a more representative evidence base for adaptation and resilience planning in African cities.

Flooding and heat-related topics dominate the literature, whereas sea-level rise, windstorms and urban water stress receive comparatively limited attention. Consideration of multiple hazards remains limited and uneven, while explicit analysis of interactions between hazards is rare. Earth Observation is widely used, but its broader potential remains underexploited, while high-resolution urban climate modelling and observations remain limited. Most studies focus on historical or present-day conditions, and few combine future climate scenarios with projected urban growth. Overall, broader geographic and thematic coverage, improved high-resolution observations and urban-scale modelling, and stronger integration of future climate and urban development are needed to provide a more representative evidence base for adaptation and resilience planning in African cities.

articles.title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
articles.titleEn: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
articles.abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

articles.title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
articles.titleEn: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
articles.abstract: Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na + ) and potassium (K + ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na + and K + ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

articles.title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe 2
articles.titleEn: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe 2
articles.abstract: Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe 2 /LiAl 2 Fe 3 O 8 (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe 2 /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe 2 . The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe 2 . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

articles.title: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
articles.titleEn: How high-pressure ices on large ocean worlds can support habitability: The compatibility of amino acids into ice VI and VII
articles.abstract: Water oceans in large icy moons and exoplanets are isolated from the rocky interior by thick layers of high-pressure ice, which hinder the direct release of nutrients and organics derived from water-rock interaction to the ocean. Possible uptake of these bio-essential compounds into high-pressure ice phases could regulate their availability in the ocean, but this process is poorly constrained. Here, we measured partition coefficients of glycine and alanine into ices VI and VII under elevated temperature-pressure conditions using a diamond-anvil cell. We observed moderate compatibility of glycine and alanine with partition coefficients: K p ,glycine = 0.14 and 0.40 in ices VI and VII, respectively; K p ,alanine = 0.21 and 0.35 in ices VI and VII, respectively. First-principles calculations suggested that amino acids could be incorporated into high-pressure ice’s lattice via cogrowth. Compatibility of amino acids into high-pressure ices would favor their transport in large extraterrestrial oceans, opening an avenue to habitability.

articles.title: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
articles.titleEn: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
articles.abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states—a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

articles.title: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
articles.titleEn: Climatic niche conservatism shapes the macroevolution, extinction, and survivorship of crocodile-line archosaurs
articles.abstract: Crocodylians are iconic thermophiles. Over 250 million years, crocodile-line archosaurs endured hyperthermals, climatic and range shifts, and two mass extinctions. Whether this niche conservatism reflects a deep evolutionary constraint or recent adaptation to novel climates remains unclear. We integrate present-day occurrences with a time-scaled phylogeny of >400 fossil and extant species. Niche models calibrated on living crocodylians were projected across 245 million years and compared with paleophylogeographic reconstructions. Macroevolutionary model fitting shows that temperature and precipitation exhibit strong phylogenetic structure, best described by bounded Ornstein-Uhlenbeck dynamics, indicating long-term niche conservatism. Poleward expansions in warm intervals and contractions in cool phases reflect tracking of conserved optima rather than niche evolution. Unlike non-avian dinosaurs, low-latitude suitability persisted across all but the most extreme end-Cretaceous scenarios, with recovery expanding from tropical refugia. Thermal and precipitation regimes shifted near the Cenomanian/Turonian hyperthermal (∼93.9 Ma) and Eocene/Oligocene aridification transition (∼33.9 Ma), respectively. Climatic niche conservatism is therefore ancient in crocodile-line archosaurs, but not completely static.

articles.title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
articles.titleEn: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
articles.abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

articles.title: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
articles.titleEn: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
articles.abstract: Arginine methylation regulates diverse cellular processes, yet how methyl-arginine reader proteins couple this modification to kinase signaling in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we identify staphylococcal nuclease and Tudor domain containing 1 (SND1) as a pancreas-enriched effector that links symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) recognition to S6 kinase 2 (S6K2) activation. Disruption of SDMA-mediated binding by a point mutation in the SND1 Tudor domain markedly diminishes ribosomal protein S6 (S6) phosphorylation in the pancreas. Mechanistically, SND1 engages SDMA-modified arginines within the carboxyl-terminal glycine-arginine–rich (GAR) motif of S6K2 and promotes S6K2-dependent S6 phosphorylation. Mice harboring lysine substitutions at these GAR arginines ( S6k2 RK) phenocopy Snd1 Tudor-mutant ( Snd1 knock-in) animals, exhibiting impaired pancreatic S6 phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses reveal extensive overlap in dysregulated pathways between Snd1 and S6k2 mutant pancreata, supporting a shared signaling cascade. Together, these findings establish a methylation-dependent reader-kinase axis that links protein arginine methyltransferase 5–catalyzed arginine methylation to tissue-specific control of ribosome signaling and cellular stress adaptation.

articles.title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
articles.titleEn: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
articles.abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

articles.title: How Urban–Rural Integration Reshapes the Carbon Source‐Sink Balance: A Carbon Offset‐Based Analysis Revealing Pathways and Scale Effects
articles.titleEn: How Urban–Rural Integration Reshapes the Carbon Source‐Sink Balance: A Carbon Offset‐Based Analysis Revealing Pathways and Scale Effects
articles.abstract: The transition toward carbon neutrality is critically shaped by the management of urban–rural interactions, yet the net carbon consequences of urban–rural integration (URI) remain poorly understood. We systematically assess how URI reshapes the carbon source‐sink balance via an integrated multi‐step analytical approach for 335 Chinese cities (2005–2020). We employ the carbon offset effect (COE)—the net balance between vegetation carbon sequestration (CS) and energy‐related emissions—as a key indicator. We reveal a persistent spatial mismatch between URI advancement and carbon sink capacity, with the national carbon deficit widening from 4.65 to 9.5 Gt CO 2 and the share of emissions offset by vegetation CS falling from 21.98% to 10.41%. Crucially, we identify two competing pathways: A structural optimization pathway associated with improved carbon outcomes, and a spatial squeeze pathway associated with degraded carbon outcomes. The spatial squeeze pathway dominates, as the standardized coefficient of land urbanization level ( β = −0.493) is 6.49 times larger in absolute magnitude than that of the structural optimization pathway ( β = 0.076). The negative association between URI and vegetation COE exhibits scale‐dependent heterogeneity, weakening at higher integration levels and in larger cities, while local synergies between development and carbon sinks are attainable in some key ecological function areas. Our findings reveal the complex relationship between urban–rural transitions and terrestrial carbon dynamics, challenging the assumption that regional integration inherently yields ecological co‐benefits. Incorporating a net carbon‐impact lens into spatial planning is essential to unlock the climate mitigation potential of urban–rural systems, a lesson critical for rapidly urbanizing regions globally.

articles.title: Scalable Phase‐Field Implementation of Crack Evolution (SPICE) for Modeling Surface Crevasse Growth and Interaction in Glaciers
articles.titleEn: Scalable Phase‐Field Implementation of Crack Evolution (SPICE) for Modeling Surface Crevasse Growth and Interaction in Glaciers
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Iceberg calving driven by crevasse propagation is an important source of ice loss from the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets. However, simulating crevasse growth and interaction in 3D, spanning meters to kilometers length scales, remains computationally challenging for high‐fidelity models based on nonlocal continuum damage mechanics and phase‐field fracture approaches. The high computational cost of high‐fidelity models comes from the need to adequately resolve the damage/phase‐field length scale (often meters in scale) within the finite element method to capture complex crevasse patterns and interactions, involving stress redistribution, shielding, and coalescence. To overcome this difficulty, a scalable parallel implementation for crack evolution is developed using the open‐source finite element software FEniCS, which features a novel recursively adaptive mesh refinement (RAMR) algorithm to solve the stress‐based phase‐field fracture model equations in 3D. The RAMR algorithm automatically refines the mesh in the fracture process zones based on the phase field variable and a user‐defined finest cell size to capture crack propagation and coalescence accurately and efficiently. Idealized simulations of kilometer‐scale glacier domains show 13‐ to 45‐fold speedup compared to locally refined meshes, with less than 2% discrepancy in crevasse depth. This computational efficiency enables kilometer‐scale simulations of a field of closely spaced crevasses showcasing arcuate paths and crisscross patterns, resembling field and remotely‐sensed observations of glacier crevasses. The simulations also reveal that crevasse growth is predominantly governed by tensile principal stresses, which are determined by the initial crevasse spacing and margin boundary conditions.

articles.title: Simulating Carbon Emission Dynamics in Agricultural Drainage Ditches: Development and Evaluation of the PCDitch‐Carbon Model
articles.titleEn: Simulating Carbon Emission Dynamics in Agricultural Drainage Ditches: Development and Evaluation of the PCDitch‐Carbon Model
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: With their high abundance in agricultural landscapes, drainage ditches are important components of the global water cycle and potential carbon (CO 2 and CH 4 ) emission hotspots. However, explicit process‐based estimates of carbon emissions from these systems are lacking, with ditch biogeochemical complexity being a major constraining factor. To fill this gap, we developed PCDitch‐Carbon, a carbon emission model, from the well‐established process‐based ditch ecosystem model PCDitch. Our research goals were to (a) identify key parameters that affect carbon emissions using sensitivity analysis, (b) determine the responses in carbon emissions to external nutrient loading using bifurcation analysis and (c) validate the predicted carbon emissions with empirical observations. Sensitivity analysis highlighted hydromorphology, external nutrient and carbon loadings, and ecological states (submerged macrophyte vs. Lemnid dominated vegetation) as key drivers of carbon emissions. Bifurcation analysis showed decreased CO 2 and increased CH 4 emissions with external nutrient loading. Additionally, hysteresis related to ecological state was observed underlying the presence of ecological feedback loops in governing carbon emissions. Modeled emissions reflected empirical observations from 10 ditch systems reasonably well, with higher CH 4 in summer–autumn and lower in winter–spring, as well as lower CO 2 emissions during spring‐summer due to primary production. PCDitch‐Carbon demonstrates the potential of process‐based ecosystem models in understanding and predicting carbon emissions from drainage ditches. Furthermore, this study offers valuable insights into the carbon emission responses in ditch ecosystems over a nutrient loading and depth gradient, thus paving the way for assessing the effectivity of management scenarios in controlling carbon emissions from ditches.

articles.titleEn: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
articles.abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

articles.title: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
articles.titleEn: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
articles.abstract: Sea level rise (SLR) threatens terrestrial biodiversity, yet its spatiotemporal and species-specific impacts remain unclear. Integrating relative SLR projections across five shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs) with area of habitat (AOH) maps for 34,120 terrestrial vertebrate species, we project that species exposed to SLR will increase from up to 13,680 in 2050 to 15,324 by 2100, including 57 to 63% of birds, 47 to 52% of mammals, 28 to 36% of reptiles, and 20 to 24% of amphibians. In Southeast Asia, inland inundation areas support high richness. Under SSP5-8.5, species facing >10% habitat inundation surge from 18 in 2050 to 109 by 2100, with reptiles and already threatened species overrepresented. Safeguarding SLR refugia—the noninundated habitats for exposed species—is critical, yet more than 96% lie outside protected areas, which means that early international action is required.

articles.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
articles.titleEn: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
articles.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

articles.title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
articles.titleEn: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

articles.title: The AI debate is missing half the system
articles.titleEn: The AI debate is missing half the system
articles.abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

articles.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
articles.titleEn: Sequential diagnosis with language models
articles.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

articles.title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.titleEn: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

articles.title: Superlubricity by glycerosome boundary layers
articles.titleEn: Superlubricity by glycerosome boundary layers
articles.abstract: The search for high-performance lubricants is of broad relevance to biomedical applications, including artificial joints, regenerative scaffolds, and osteoarthritis therapies. Here we introduce glycerosomes—phosphatidylcholine (PC)-based vesicles containing glycerol—as a promising boundary lubricant. Using a surface force balance, we show that glycerosomes achieve a friction coefficient as low as 10 − 5 under a high compression pressure of 15.6 MPa, representing a 20-fold reduction compared to conventional PC liposomes. This level of lubrication surpasses any previously reported boundary lubricant system at such pressures in aqueous media. Mechanistically, glycerosomes exhibit substantially lower adhesion energy than PC liposomes, and theoretical simulations reveal enhanced vesicle stability and flexibility. Our findings establish glycerosomes as a superior hydration lubrication platform, with promising implications for both biomedical implants and industrial applications requiring robust lubricity.

articles.title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
articles.titleEn: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
articles.abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

articles.title: Exploring Climate Change Effects on Concurrent Floods and Concurrent Droughts via Statistical Deep Learning
articles.titleEn: Exploring Climate Change Effects on Concurrent Floods and Concurrent Droughts via Statistical Deep Learning
articles.abstract: Concurrent floods and concurrent droughts in nearby catchments pose challenges to risk assessment and water management. Climate change is affecting extremely high and low discharge, but the complex interplay between changes in individual catchments, and in the dependence across catchments, make it difficult to provide accurate assessments of the occurrence probabilities of concurrent extremes. In this work, we use a contemporary statistical deep learning model to capture concurrent river floods and droughts in four catchments in the Upper Danube basin, based on discharge simulated by a hydrological model driven with large ensemble climate model output. The statistical model is able to accurately capture the tail behavior of the simulated discharge, which we assess by making use of the large available sample. We subsequently use our statistical model to study changes in joint tail behavior of discharge over time, finding that both compound flooding and drought‐like conditions are becoming increasingly likely toward the end of the 21st century under a high‐emission scenario. In particular, our results highlight that changes in the dependence structure of extremes strongly contribute to the detected changes, an aspect that would be difficult to capture with traditional approaches. This work paves the way for highly flexible, general inference on compound extremes in hydrological applications, and demonstrates key advantages of using statistical deep learning in this setting.

articles.title: Four Decades of Reach‐Scale Declines in Total Phosphorus Across the Yellow River Basin Driven by Vegetation Restoration and Dam Impoundment
articles.titleEn: Four Decades of Reach‐Scale Declines in Total Phosphorus Across the Yellow River Basin Driven by Vegetation Restoration and Dam Impoundment
articles.abstract: Phosphorus (P) is a finite resource fundamental to terrestrial and aquatic productivity. However, excessive P transfer from land to rivers threatens food production and degrades water quality. Systematic analyses of multidecadal total phosphorus (TP) variation in large river basins remain challenging because of incomplete and non‐uniform observational data. Here, we develop a potentially transferable and generalizable framework combining remote sensing and machine learning to reconstruct long‐term and reach‐scale TP variation in the Yellow River Basin from 1986 to 2024, based on synchronous multimodal and in situ data ( N = 1,490). The results confirm that the framework can reliably estimate TP concentration, achieving Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency = 0.71 and root mean squared error = 27.1 μg L −1 on the test set. TP concentration shows a significant temporal decline in 55% of river reaches; spatial heterogeneity is evident, with concentrations in the middle reaches declining most rapidly at 4.1 μg L −1 per decade. However, TP flux (TPF) exhibits a U‐shaped temporal trajectory, increasing after 2015 as river discharge rises; the spatial gradient follows a hump‐shaped pattern, characterized by a peak of 2,094 t yr −1 at Tongguan. Vegetation restoration reduces land‐to‐river TP export, and dam impoundment impedes in‐stream TP transport, both of which largely account for the declines in TP concentration in the Yellow River Basin. This study proposes a potentially generalizable framework for riverine TP reconstruction at high spatial resolution over multiple decades and provides new insights into the anthropogenic impact on TP dynamics in big river systems.

articles.title: Analysis of Dual‐Porosity Model With Fissure Skin Effect in Confined Karst Aquifer
articles.titleEn: Analysis of Dual‐Porosity Model With Fissure Skin Effect in Confined Karst Aquifer
articles.abstract: In fractured media with rough fissure skins, ignoring the fissure skin effect limits the accuracy of parameter inversion. In karst aquifers, groundwater storage and movement are typically governed by dual‐porosity models, where the fissure skin plays a key role in water exchange between fissures and the rock matrix. articles.title: Auto‐STIV: A Deep Learning Framework for Fully Autonomous Two‐Dimensional Streamflow Velocity Vector Field Estimation
articles.titleEn: Auto‐STIV: A Deep Learning Framework for Fully Autonomous Two‐Dimensional Streamflow Velocity Vector Field Estimation
articles.abstract: Accurate and continuous streamflow monitoring can support effective water resource management, yet substantial gaps persist in national streamgage networks due to operational challenges and costs. Non‐contact, image‐based techniques such as Space‐Time Image Velocimetry (STIV) offer a safe, scalable and, cost‐effective alternative for measuring surface flow velocity in rivers, which allows for streamflow calculation, especially during hazardous flood events. Traditional STIV methods, however, often require manual parameter tuning and struggle with complex flow conditions. This study introduces Auto‐STIV, a novel deep learning framework that fully automates the estimation of both flow direction and velocity magnitude from video imagery. The proposed approach utilizes a two‐stage Convolutional Neural Network model. The first stage predicts the primary flow direction by analyzing a stack of Space‐Time Images (STIs) generated from a series of candidate orientations. The second stage estimates the velocity magnitude from the STI corresponding to the predicted direction. The model was trained on a comprehensive data set collected under diverse, controlled laboratory conditions and evaluated using real‐world footage from the Colorado River. Results demonstrate that Auto‐STIV outperforms the traditional autocorrelation‐based STIV method, exhibiting higher accuracy and greater robustness in the presence of challenging environmental factors such as variable lighting, low‐contrast surface textures, and complex flow patterns. This research underscores the potential of deep learning to enhance the capabilities of image‐based velocimetry, that may support more reliable, scalable, and automated streamflow monitoring systems.
